profile.description: Vertiv designs, manufactures, installs and services critical digital infrastructure (power, thermal and related hardware, software and services) primarily for data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial environments.

segments.sells: Critical digital infrastructure hardware, software and services
segments.end_markets: Data centers, communication networks, commercial and industrial customers in the Americas

segments.name: Asia Pacific
segments.sells: Critical digital infrastructure hardware, software and services
segments.end_markets: Data centers, communication networks, commercial and industrial customers in Asia Pacific

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.sells: Critical digital infrastructure hardware, software and services
segments.end_markets: Data centers, communication networks, commercial and industrial customers in EMEA

geography.summary: Segments are geographic. 2025 net sales of $10,229.9 million were 62% Americas, 20% Asia Pacific and 18% EMEA (about $6.39B, $2.02B and $1.82B excluding intercompany sales).

evidence.quote: We manage our business across three reportable segments based on our main geographic regions
of which 62% was transacted in the Americas; 20% was transacted in Asia Pacific; and 18% was transacted in Europe, Middle East & Africa.
Excluding intercompany sales, net sales were $6,386.3 in the Americas, $2,019.2 in Asia Pacific and $1,824.4 in Europe, Middle East & Africa.

customers.summary: Customers are data center, communication network and commercial and industrial operators, reached directly and through channel partners, distributors, IT resellers and value-added retailers.

evidence.quote: We design, manufacture and service critical digital infrastructure technology primarily for data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial environments.
We also utilize a robust network of channel partners, distributors, IT resellers, and value-added retailers.

backlog.latest: $15.0 billion combined order backlog at December 31, 2025 (vs $7.2 billion at December 31, 2024)
backlog.horizon: Majority considered firm and expected to ship within the next 12 to 18 months (no exact share)
backlog.summary: Backlog roughly doubled year over year; the filing cautions it is not necessarily indicative of future net sales.

evidence.quote: estimated combined order backlog was approximately $15.0 billion and $7.2 billion, respectively.
The majority of the combined backlog as of December 31, 2025 is considered firm and is expected to be shipped within the next 12 to 18 months.
The backlog consists of product and services for which a customer purchase order or purchase commitment has been received and which has not yet been delivered.

pricing.summary: The company is advancing a pricing plan and notes that, because of its large backlog, pricing changes take longer to show in results. Competition is on reliability, quality, price, service and relationships; tariffs and input costs have risen.

evidence.quote: We continue to take action to enhance our supply chain, such as qualifying new suppliers, and advancing our pricing plan.
Also, due to our large backlog, pricing changes may take longer to be reflected in our financial results.
In the past few years, we experienced significant increases in material, freight and labor costs and custom duties and tariffs.

margin_drivers.summary: Consolidated gross margin was 36.3% in 2025 vs 36.6% in 2024. The filing names operational leverage, cost improvement actions and geographic mix as drivers of a segment margin increase, and product/service mix, inefficiencies and capacity build-out as drivers of margin erosion in another.

evidence.quote: Gross profit was $3,715.2 in 2025, or 36.3% of sales, compared to $2,934.2, or 36.6% of sales in 2024.
Margin increased primarily driven by operational leverage, cost improvement actions, and geographical mix.
Margin erosion was primarily due to the mix of product and service sales, operational inefficiencies, and increased capacity to support future global demand.
